Subject: Renewal paperwork + proposed term change

Hi Laura,

Quick note as we prep our renewal: the team wants to move from a 12-month term to an 18-month term to match our budgeting cadence, and there will be an expected capacity uplift of ~40% across Q1–Q2 of next year. I've attached a marked-up MSA with the term language we propose and an updated order form with the new capacity numbers.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the price tiers will remain unchanged if we move to 18 months (we expect to keep the same per-unit price but need a formal confirmation)?
- We also have one compliance question: can you confirm retention windows for KV cache / logs under Dedicated?

If useful we can hop on a 30m call — would prefer to get legal comments in writing first.

Thanks,
Tom Nguyen
Director of Infrastructure
ClearSky Labs

Thanks Tom — looping in Ben (legal) and Mina (CS ops) to review redlines and capacity plan. High level: were supportive of moving to 18 months and a capacity uplift, but need to confirm pricing tiers and SLA adjustments for the longer term and larger baseline.

Ben / Mina — quick context: ClearSky is proposing: 18-month term, baseline capacity +40% (phased). They attached a marked MSA and an updated order form. Specific items to look for:
- Termination notice windows & auto-renew language (Tom adjusted these)
- SLA credit language for Dedicated during scaling windows
- Data retention and audit log retention windows for Dedicated (customer asks 90/365?)
- Any downstream billing proration for mid-term capacity increases

Can you review the doc and post redline notes here? If legal needs a stub for a canary or staged deployment clause (to allow fallback to hosted variants during spikes), flag it.

Ill hold on scheduling a call until we have legal/ops alignment.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@clearskylabs.com>, contracts@clearskylabs.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork + proposed term change

Laura / Mina — read through the redline. High-level legal view: we can accept an 18-month term but with three carveouts I want to flag for negotiation (tracked below). Ive attached comments inline in the doc; summarizing here for clarity:

1) Auto-renew & notice window: ClearSky shortened our standard 60-day opt-out to 30 days. We should push back to 60 days for an 18-month term or else add a mid-term review clause.

2) SLA credits for capacity scaling: theyre asking for credits tied to percent availability during ramp windows. We should accept credits tied to sustained <95% monthly availability but cap cumulative credits at 6% of monthly fees per quarter for scalability events outside our control.

3) Data retention: we cannot promise shorter-than-standard retention for customer-managed Dedicated traces (30 days recommended). We can offer 90 days of audit log retention as a paid add-on; KV cache retention is ephemeral and not part of retention guarantee.

Operational asks for Mina: confirm whether Dedicated can have a staged capacity add (phased across two quarters) and whether we need a special change-order flow for proration. If ops approves, well include an "Order Flow for Phased Uplift" exhibit in the order form.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to propose revised MSA language on auto-renew and SLA caps.
- Mina to confirm ops feasibility and provide proration language.
- We loop Tom back with a single consolidated redline and rationale.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ClearSky_Redline_MSA_v3_with_comments.docx (legal comments)

From: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@clearskylabs.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, contracts@clearskylabs.com
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork + proposed term change

Hi all,

Appreciate the quick read, Ben. We reviewed your summary and attached a narrower set of asks so we can move quickly:
- We can concede to the 60-day notice but would like a guaranteed mid-term pricing review (language suggested in redline).
- For SLA credits, ClearSky asks that credits trigger at <98% during planned ramp windows only; we can accept your 6% quarterly cap.
- For retention: ClearSky accepts the 90-day audit log add-on but requests written confirmation that Redwood will provide an export of audit logs on request within 30 days.

Attached is an updated marked MSA and a brief cover note from procurement. If you can consolidate the final redline and share a DocuSign link for signature, wed prefer to wrap this up by next week.

Tom
Director of Infrastructure
ClearSky Labs
